# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.

# Intake Brief — Enhance Central AI boss encounter

**Work item:** Enhance Central AI boss encounter: 200 HP, more minions, figure-8 movement, top-screen health bar, hit feedback (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X)

## Problem statement

The Central AI boss encounter is currently a static, 400-hit grind: the boss does not move, the health bar is drawn relative to the boss container (so it is visibly displaced rather than at the top of the screen), and individual hits give no feedback beyond a bullet disappearing. Players cannot read their progress and the fight lacks the mobility and impact expected of a climactic boss. This work item reduces the boss's total health to **200**, reinforces the fight with **more minions**, gives the boss **figure-of-8 movement**, fixes the **health bar to the top of the screen**, and makes **every hit obvious through SFX and VFX**.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** fights the boss after clearing Level 5 and wants a readable, impactful, mobile encounter.
  - *As a player, I want to see the boss's health decrease with every hit so I know my shots are registering.*
  - *As a player, I want the fight to feel dynamic and dangerous, with the boss moving and more enemies on screen.*
  - *As a player, I want clear audio/visual feedback on each hit so the encounter feels responsive.*
- **Developer/maintainer (secondary):** wants the change implemented once in the shared core so the game and boss gyms stay in parity.
  - *As a developer, I want the boss behaviour to live in the shared core so `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
2. **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
3. **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
4. **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
5. **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
6. **Test coverage.** New/updated tests cover the health model, minion counts, figure-8 motion, health-bar placement, and hit feedback across `Boss.test.ts`, `BossMinions.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts`, `PlayScene.test.ts`, and the audio cue contract.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the Game Design Document (§4.3), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 parity), and the audio cue mapping/manifest.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (mandatory):** gameplay behaviour must live in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/entities/`) and be consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss`; no divergent copies. The `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must still pass.
- **Preserve the 4-phase model:** do not change the phase attack patterns, telegraphs, or reward gating; only retune totals/counts and add movement/feedback.
- **Health bar model:** keep the existing proportional `getHpFraction()` fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
- **Audio pipeline:** a new SFX cue must be registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` and `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` (the contract test enforces completeness).
- **No new dependencies.**
- Stay within the existing visual/neon style and UK-English documentation conventions.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: 4 phases × `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` = **400 total hits**; `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`; `healthBarGraphics` is added as a **child of the boss container** but drawn with screen coordinates (so it renders offset by the boss position); `takeDamage()` only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit; no per-hit feedback.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`: phase 1 = 8 scouts (4+4), phase 2 = 8 divers (4+4), phase 3 = 0, phase 4 = 10 swarm.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_damageBoss()`: applies damage and awards score/summons minions on phase depletion; no hit SFX/VFX.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` `damageBoss()`: gym equivalent, mirrors the game's gating.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss()`: shared per-frame boss advance consumed by both the game and the gym (the correct place for shared movement/feedback).
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`: reusable `spawnBulletImpact()` flash already used for non-lethal hits on multi-hit enemies (Harvester) but **not** wired to the boss.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`: no boss-hit cue exists.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.3 documents the 400-hit model and static boss.

## Desired change

1. Retune boss health to a **200-hit total** (4 phases × 50) and update the constants/comments/tests.
2. Increase minion counts to **P1 = 12, P2 = 12, P3 = 0, P4 = 15**.
3. Add **figure-8 (lemniscate) movement** around the spawn anchor in the shared boss core, with parameters ≈120 px / ≈60 px / ≈8 s, bounded to the playfield.
4. **Re-parent the health bar** out of the boss container so it is camera-fixed at the top-centre of the screen, always visible, and unaffected by boss movement; keep the proportional fill and phase dividers.
5. Add a **dedicated boss-hit SFX cue** and an **obvious hit VFX** (impact flash/burst at the hit point) applied on every hit through a shared path used by both the game and the gym; keep the existing phase-transition feedback.
6. Update tests and documentation (GDD, enemy design/parity doc, audio mapping).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — health constants (50/phase, 200 total), figure-8 movement, health-bar re-parenting/positioning, per-hit feedback hook.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` — increased per-phase minion counts.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared boss movement/feedback seam for parity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring; health-bar layering.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring (parity).
- `src/audio/effects.ts`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — new boss-hit cue and mapping.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — reusable/extended impact flash for boss hits.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/waves/BossMinions.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed) — established the `phaseAdvanced`-gated score/minion behaviour this work preserves.
- **AH-0MUUJCL8J00632T7** – Boss.ts per-phase HP model, return contract, health-bar fill (completed) — the `getHpFraction()` proportional fill this work keeps.
- **AH-0MUTV3J7T006MZ4K** – Increase Central AI boss hits-per-phase 10x (completed) — prior health tuning precedent.
- **AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE** – Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (completed) — gym that must stay in parity.
- **AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ** – Integrate boss encounter into PlayScene (completed) — boss spawn wiring and minion sums.
- **AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I** – Extract collision core and host bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback (completed) — shared impact-feedback precedent.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed)
- **AH-0MU3X86GT001YM5D** – Identify enemy refactor opportunities (completed)
- **AH-0MUUJFOTM009ORQM** – GDD and code comment documentation updates (AC7) (completed)

Repository file matches: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "200 health" means 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each), not 200 per phase.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** minion increase ≈50% in phases 1, 2 and 4; phase 3 stays minion-free.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** figure-8 defaults 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s; boss-only motion; top-centre screen-fixed health bar; new per-hit SFX + impact-flash VFX.
- **Risk:** figure-8 motion could push the boss off-screen or desync aimed shots/minions — mitigate with bounded amplitude and using the boss's live position for aiming/collision.
- **Risk:** health-bar re-parenting may break tests that assume the bar is a container child — update those tests and add explicit screen-position assertions.
- **Risk:** the new SFX may need a ToneForge recipe/baked asset; if a new recipe is required the audio build pipeline must render it (or reuse an existing recipe) and the manifest must stay complete so the contract test passes.
- **Risk:** gameplay change requires parity across `PlayScene` and all boss gyms — implement in shared core only; verify with the equivalence/parity tests.
- **Scope-creep:** further boss rebalancing (attack patterns, telegraph timings, additional phases) is out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What does "reduce the health to 200" mean?** Options: (a) 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each); (b) 200 per phase (800 total); (c) other. **Recommended:** (a) — preserves the 4-phase model.
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2: How much should the minion count increase, and in which phases?** Options: (a) ~50% more in phases 1, 2 and 4 (P1 12, P2 12, P3 0, P4 15); (b) roughly double all; (c) add minions to phase 3; (d) other. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3: Are the implementation defaults acceptable?** (figure-8: 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s, boss-only; hit feedback: new hit SFX + impact flash on every hit, keeping phase-transition feedback; health bar: screen-fixed top-centre). **Recommended:** accept.
  - **Answer (operator):** "yes". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

# Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

## Problem statement

When the hold fills and the player is offered a choice of upgrades, owned upgrades (weapon-level / power-up-level options) should appear 10% more likely than they currently do. Currently all candidates are selected uniformly at random; owned upgrades should receive a 1.1× weight multiplier.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when offered a hold-full choice I want a reasonable chance of upgrading an upgradeable weapon or power-up I already own, so my build keeps improving rather than forcing me to chase new items."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want owned upgrades to appear 10% more often so progression feels steady across runs."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 10% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (both `weapon-level` and `power-up-level`) have a 1.1× weight multiplier applied during candidate selection. Unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0× weight.
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The weighting logic lives in the strategy layer (`createRandomChoiceStrategy`), not in `buildChoiceCandidates`; no duplicate weighting code in scenes or gyms.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`.
- **AC4 — Configurable weight.** The 1.1× multiplier is a named constant (e.g. `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1`) so it can be tuned later without hunting for magic numbers.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify: (a) owned-level candidates receive 1.1× weight; (b) weighted random selection produces the expected distribution (10,000 trials, ±3% tolerance, owned items appear ~10% more often than unowned items relative to pool size); (c) gym↔game parity tests pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once and be consumed by both the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy` interface or existing `ChoiceOption` consumers.
- **No gameplay logic changes beyond weighting:** the candidate list itself is unchanged — only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add weighting logic in `createRandomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — no changes expected (they already pass context).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — new tests for weighted selection (10k trials, ±3%).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — parity tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship'\''s hold (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Statistical testing (low):** proving 10% bias requires many trials; tests use 10,000 draws with ±3% tolerance band.
- **Scope creep (low):** adding per-weight tunability (player-facing weight editor) could expand scope. Mitigation: this item implements a single constant only; per-weight tuning is a separate chore if needed.
- **Assumption:** "10% more likely" means a 1.1× multiplicative weight, not an additive 10 percentage points.
- **Assumption:** "owned upgrade" means `weapon-level` and `power-up-level` kind options in the candidate list.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of owned upgrades?** (A: both weapon-level and power-up-level; B: only weapon-level; C: both with different weights.) — Answer (Producer): A — both weapon-level and power-up-level.
- **Q2 — Where does weighting logic live?** (A: in `buildChoiceCandidates` with tagged weights; B: in `createRandomChoiceStrategy` strategy layer.) — Answer (Producer): B — in the strategy layer.
- **Q3 — Test tolerance for statistical validation?** (A: 10,000 trials, ±3%; B: 50,000 trials, ±1%; C: 5,000 trials, ±5%.) — Answer (Producer): A — 10,000 trials, ±3%.

# Intake Brief — Bot is more gentle on the thrusters (AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A)

## Problem statement

The attract/demo bot's human-like thrust layer holds every forward-thrust press
for a fixed random band (200–225 ms normally, up to 400 ms on a long-travel
leg). This makes the bot's thruster "on" runs a little longer than a human's
and contributes to a slightly mechanical, over-eager feel. The producer wants
the bot to be a little gentler on the thrusters by shortening each press's
**on** time by a random **1–5%**.

## Users

- **Attract-mode viewer / operator:** watches the demo run and perceives the
  bot as a believable human pilot rather than a thruster-abusing machine.
- **Gameplay designers:** tune bot feel through one shared module without
  hunting for magic numbers.

Example user stories:

- *As an operator watching the attract demo, I want the bot to make slightly
  shorter, less mechanical thrust bursts, so that the demo reads as human play.*
- *As a designer, I want the gentle-thrust reduction to be a single documented
  tunable pair, so that I can adjust the feel without touching the governor
  logic.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each forward-thrust press duration is reduced by a random factor drawn
  uniformly from **1%–5%** (inclusive of the configured bounds). With the
  default caps this shortens a normal press from the 200–225 ms band to
  ≈190–222.75 ms and a long-travel press from the 400 ms cap to ≈380 ms;
  unit-tested.
- AC2: The reduction is drawn **per press** and is reproducible for a given
  governor seed (a run-seeded governor produces an identical reduction
  sequence across two instances with the same seed); unit-tested.
- AC3: Continuous desired thrust still holds the thruster **on** for every tick
  (the reduction must not introduce off-gaps); existing continuous-thrust test
  remains green.
- AC4: The reduction bounds live in the shared `BotHumanInputTunables` module
  (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) as documented min/max percent tunables with
  defaults `0.01`/`0.05`; no scattered magic numbers.
- AC5: Documentation is updated to describe the gentler thrust — the demo-bot
  subsection in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and the `botHumanLike.ts`
  module doc both note the 1–5% random reduction of press "on" time.
- AC6: At least one new automated test validates the reduction band and
  per-press randomness; full project test suite, typecheck and build must pass
  with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the change surgical: only the thrust-press duration draw is affected;
  the chosen heading/target, reaction cadence, W/A/D key limits, and
  forward-model braking reflex are unchanged.
- No new dependency; keep the deterministic mulberry32 RNG already used for
  per-press jitter (do not introduce `Math.random()`).
- The reduction must be a *reduction only* (never extend a press), so the bot
  becomes gentler, not more aggressive.
- Single source of truth for tunables (`BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`).

## Existing state

`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` implements the human-like input governor. In
`BotInputGovernor.resolveThrustPress`, a new press duration is drawn as:

```ts
const maxMs = longTravel ? thrustPressMaxMsLong : thrustPressMaxMs;
const span = Math.max(0, maxMs - thrustPressMinMs);
this.thrustPressRemainingMs = thrustPressMinMs + this.random() * span;
```

Defaults: `thrustPressMinMs: 200`, `thrustPressMaxMs: 225`,
`thrustPressMaxMsLong: 400`. The drawn duration is the thruster's "on" time.
`resolveThrustPress` is unit-tested in `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`
(`human-like thrust presses (AC15/AC16)` suite), and the GDD demo-bot
subsection documents the 200–225 / 400 ms bands.

## Desired change

After drawing the base press duration, apply a per-press random reduction of
1–5%:

```ts
const baseMs = thrustPressMinMs + this.random() * span;
const reduction =
  thrustPressGentleMinPct +
  this.random() * (thrustPressGentleMaxPct - thrustPressGentleMinPct);
this.thrustPressRemainingMs = baseMs * (1 - reduction);
```

Add the two bounds to `BotHumanInputTunables` and
`BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`, document them, and update the GDD demo-bot
subsection and module doc.

**Interpretation note (documented assumption):** the phrase *"reduce their
'on' time by between 1 and 5% (random)"* is read as reducing each thrust-press
**hold duration** by a per-press random 1–5%. This is the only "on" time in
the bot's thrust path. The alternative reading — inserting random off-gaps
into the thrust duty cycle — is explicitly **out of scope** for this item and
recorded as a risk below; the producer can request it during review.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — add `thrustPressGentleMinPct` /
  `thrustPressGentleMaxPct` tunables and apply the per-press reduction in
  `resolveThrustPress`; update module/documentation comments.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts` — extend the "human-like thrust presses"
  suite with reduction-band and per-press-randomness/determinism tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — demo-bot subsection: note the 1–5% random
  reduction of thrust-press on-time.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — Demo bot: human-like input limits (W/A/D, reaction
  time) and complete the hold-full upgrade choice** (completed) — introduced
  the governor, the human reaction cadence, and the 200–225 / 400 ms thrust
  press bands this item tunes.
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L — Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups >
  enemies > asteroids** (completed) — the steering/priority behaviour that
  produces the thrust decisions.
- **AH-0MUY08V6W001SJJN — Deterministic run seeding and seed plumbing**
  (completed) — the run seed that re-seeds the governor's per-press RNG, which
  keeps the new reduction deterministic per run.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` § demo/attract bot ("Predictive braking
  (AC10)" bullet) — documents the current thrust-press durations.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (interpretation):** "on time" = thrust-press hold duration
  (see Desired change). If the producer intended a duty-cycle gap instead,
  this item's scope is wrong and should be re-defined before implementation.
- **Risk — negligible visible effect:** because a press is continuously
  renewed while the live `thrust` flag stays `true`, the reduction mainly
  shortens the *overhang* after the forward model decides to coast. A 1–5%
  change is deliberately subtle; the demo may need an audition to confirm the
  feel is meaningfully gentler. Mitigation: make the bounds tunable so the
  band can be widened without a code change.
- **Risk — scope creep:** while in the governor it is tempting to also retune

## Goal

As a producer, I want `npm run capture` to record multiple gameplay clips in a single invocation, so that collecting a batch of N clips does not require an external bash loop that re-boots the Vite dev server, re-warms the game and re-installs Playwright bookkeeping on every iteration.

## Context

`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (see `package.json` script `capture`) currently records exactly **one** clip per invocation. The output path defaults to `capture-output/gameplay-<ISO-timestamp>.webm` (ms precision) or an explicit `--output`. There is no `--count`/`-n` flag.

Current workaround is a shell loop:

```bash
for i in {1..50}; do npm run capture || break; done
```

This works but is slow (each run boots its own dev server, warmup, then a full run + tail) and cannot reuse a kept server (`--keep-server`) across iterations cleanly.

## Expected behaviour

- New flag `--count <n>` with alias `-n <n>`, defaulting to `1` (preserving existing behaviour).
- The script performs `n` capture iterations in one process, reusing the dev server and browser resources where practical.
- Each iteration writes its own file; when `--output` is not supplied, continue using the timestamped default naming and guarantee uniqueness across iterations (e.g. include the iteration index / suffix, since same-ms timestamps collide within a tight loop).
- When `--output` **is** supplied with `--count > 1`, either reject the combination with a clear error or infer an indexed suffix (`demo-1.webm`, `demo-2.webm`, ...) — pick one and document it in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the script's usage comment.
- `--scripted`, `--scenario`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup` apply to every iteration.
- `--json` reports one result object per iteration (or an array) with the produced files/probes.
- A failure in one iteration must be attributable: the summary must name the failing iteration, and the exit code must be non-zero (document whether later iterations are skipped or continued).

## Suggested implementation approach

- Extend `parseCaptureArgs` (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`) with `--count`/`-n`, validated as a positive integer.
- Wrap the existing single-capture flow in an iteration loop that keeps the server/browser alive between iterations where safe (reload rather than relaunch, if the run-end signal allows).
- Extend the output-path resolver to always produce unique names for multi-iteration runs.
- Update `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the script header usage block.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run capture -- --count 3` produces 3 distinct non-trivial `.webm` files in `capture-output/` and exits 0.
- [ ] `-n` is accepted as an alias for `--count`.
- [ ] Omitting `--count` behaves exactly as today (single clip).
- [ ] `--count` with a non-positive / non-numeric value fails fast with a clear message and non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Multi-iteration runs reuse a single dev server (no repeated boot per iteration) — verified by log/probe evidence or a test.
- [ ] `--output` + `--count > 1` behaviour is deterministic, documented and covered by a test.
- [ ] `--json` output reports per-iteration results including file paths.
- [ ] `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents `--count`/`-n` and the output-naming rules.
- [ ] Unit tests cover arg parsing (default, valid, invalid, alias) and the multi-output path resolver.

# Screen Action Intensity Tracking and Analysis

**Work item:** Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)
**Type:** task (research/decision) · **Priority:** high · **Stage:** intake

> **Headline:** AI_Hell has no recorded measure of on-screen action. This work item researches how games have tracked action/excitement intensity, decides on an approach (with a refined weighed scoring model and output schema), and creates the implementation epic — it makes no runtime changes itself.

## Problem statement

AI_Hell has no way to measure, record or reason about how much action is on
screen during a run. Designers cannot see where a run is boring or
unreadably crowded, pacing systems have no signal to react to, and the
existing gameplay-capture pipeline cannot automatically identify exciting
moments for highlight clips. We need a recorded, timestamped measure of
on-screen activity — and a researched decision on how best to compute it.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a game designer**, I can view a time-series of on-screen action
  intensity for a run, so I can evaluate pacing and identify boring or
  over-crowded segments.
- **As a game designer**, I can feed action-intensity data into future pacing
  / adaptive-difficulty work so the game maintains engaging but readable
  gameplay.
- **As a video editor**, I can use action-intensity timestamps to
  automatically select highlight clips from captured gameplay.
- **As a player**, action tracking does not affect gameplay behaviour or
  frame rate, and is not shipped enabled in production unless opted in.
- **As a maintainer**, the recording reuses the shared telemetry pipeline
  rather than introducing a parallel, drifting instrumentation path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Research & decision document exists.** A document under `docs/dev/`
   surveys how action/excitement intensity has been tracked in games (past
   and present) and compares **at least three** approaches, with a clear,
   justified recommendation for AI_Hell.
2. **Scoring model defined and refined.** The document defines the object
   categories, a weighed scoring formula (refining the seed weights:
   player/enemy bullets 1, enemies 2, enemy explosions 2, player explosions
   20, asteroids 1, upgrades 1, boss explosions 5, bosses 5), and explains
   each weight's rationale. It states how the score is aggregated, sampled
   and normalised.
3. **Output format specified.** The document defines the recorded artefact:
   its schema (timestamp, score, per-category breakdown, run seed, schema
   version), sample rate, file location/format, and how it joins to captured
   video for highlight selection.
4. **Telemetry integration stated.** The document states how the chosen
   approach integrates with / depends on the telemetry epic
   (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) and its instrumentation child
   (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH), and confirms the telemetry work item remains at
   least `high` priority.
5. **Implementation epic created.** A follow-up implementation **epic** is
   created as a **sibling** of this item (linked via
   `discovered-from:AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`), so this research item can close
   once the decision is recorded without waiting for implementation. The new
   epic records its own ACs and dependency on the telemetry items.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No gameplay change (this item).** This work item is research + decision +
  epic creation only; it must not change runtime behaviour.
- **Reuse, do not duplicate.** The existing shared core
  (`src/scenes/core/`) and telemetry effort are the canonical integration
  points; a parallel instrumentation path is prohibited by the repo
  gym↔game parity convention.
- **Cheap and bounded.** Any eventual per-tick computation must be
  O(entities) with negligible overhead, and must be a no-op when disabled.
- **Determinism-friendly.** The metric should be a pure function of scene
  state where possible, so it is reproducible from a seeded run.
- **Dev/opt-in gating.** Recording must not enter the shipped production
  bundle unless explicitly enabled (mirroring the capture pipeline's
  `import.meta.env.DEV` pattern).

## Existing state

- No action-intensity or excitement metric exists in `src/`.
- The telemetry epic (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) plans a **versioned, consent-gated,
  pluggable** pipeline recording per-tick state + input + discrete events,
  tagged with run seed and schema version. Its instrumentation child
  AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH defines a compact state vector built from the existing
  `BotSnapshot` builder — the natural place to add an `actionIntensity`
  field.
- Entities are already tracked in the shared core:
  `Player`, `Boss`, `Asteroid`, `CombatEnemyEntity`, `PlayerBullet`,
  `CombatEnemyBullet`, `CombatDrop`, plus player-explosion graphics in
  `CombatCoreScene.playerExplosions` and enemy/boss explosion VFX.
- The gameplay-capture pipeline (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`) already
  records full runs to WebM and probes "non-trivial" content via non-black
  pixel fraction, colour variety and inter-frame motion — a coarse,
  video-only proxy for action that this work would replace/augment with a
  game-logic signal.
- A pure dev-scenario resolver (`src/core/devScenario.ts`) and a dev-gated
  run-ended signal (`src/core/runEndedSignal.ts`) already exist as precedents
  for dev-only game→tooling signals.

## Desired change

Produce a decision document that selects an approach, then create the
implementation epic. The document must cover:

- **Prior art / research** (see below).
- **Alternative approaches** compared against weighted object counting.
- **A refined scoring model** with per-weight rationale.
- **The recorded artefact's schema and join semantics** for video editing.
- **Integration with the telemetry pipeline** and gym↔game parity.

## Research: prior art (seed for the decision document)

The following is the intake research summary; the decision document must
verify and expand it with citations.

### Pacing / director systems

- **Left 4 Dead AI Director (Valve, 2008)** — the canonical example. Computes
  a smoothed per-player *stress* / *intensity* from health, damage taken,
  being-attacked state and proximity, then drives horde spawns, item
  placement and adaptive music with a **build-up/release** curve. See
  Booth, *The AI Systems of Left 4 Dead* (2009).
- **Alien: Isolation (2014)**, **Back 4 Blood**, **Deep Rock Galactic** —
  descendants of the director pattern; adapt pressure to observed
  player state rather than a fixed script.
- **Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA)** — Resident Evil 4, God Hand,
  Mario Kart rubber-band AI: adapt challenge from performance metrics.

### Player-experience / affective modelling

- **Player Experience Modelling (PEM)** — Yannakakis & Hallam (2007/2009)
  model satisfaction/arousal from gameplay metrics and physiological signals
  (GSR, HR, EEG); used for real-time adaptation.
- **Psychophysiology of games** — Ravaja et al. (2006), Mandryk et al.
  (2006): event-locked EDA/ECG/EMG as ground truth for "excitement".
  Accurate but invasive; useful as *calibration* data, not runtime.

### Domain-specific density metrics

- **Bullet-hell / shmup design** — bullet density (bullets on screen, or
  bullets/second) is a standard, quantitative difficulty axis (e.g.
  Touhou/Danmakufu tooling). Directly analogous to the proposed weighted
  object count.
- **Rhythm games** — note density (notes/second) drives the star-rating
  difficulty model (osu!, StepMania).
- **RTS / esports** — Actions Per Minute (APM), supply/unit counts as
  engagement proxies.
- **Adaptive/interactive music** — Wwise/FMOD expose an *Intensity* parameter
  that scales layered music from game state; a mature, shipped precedent for
  a single scalar "action" value driving output.

### Video / highlight detection

- **NVIDIA ShadowPlay Highlights / Medal / Twitch Clips** — mostly use
  game-specific event hooks (kills) and/or audio-loudness and motion spikes.
- **Film/edit research** — action/edit intensity from shot length, motion
  vectors and audio RMS; the capture pipeline's existing probe is a crude
  version of this.

### Physics / rendering proxies

- **Kinetic-energy metrics** — sum of speed²·mass over entities as a motion
  proxy.
- **Screen entropy / edge density** — renderer-side pixel statistics; cheap
  to derive from a recording, not from game logic.

## Alternative approaches (to be compared in the decision document)

1. **Weighted on-screen object count (seed proposal).** Sum of live entity
   counts × per-type weight, sampled per tick, timestamped. Deterministic,
   cheap, reuses the telemetry state vector; weak at capturing *bursty*
   action and *threat*.
2. **Event-window intensity.** Count discrete events (shots fired, hits,
   kills, explosions, pickups) in a sliding window; captures bursts and
   moment-to-moment change, but not steady crowding.
3. **Player-stress model (AI-Director style).** Derive intensity from player
   health, recent damage, incoming-bullet proximity and nearest-enemy
   distance — measures *perceived* pressure, not raw population.
4. **Physics/motion proxy.** Sum of entity speeds (or kinetic energy) +
   projectile count; captures motion but treats harmless drift and
   threatening movement alike.
5. **Rendering/AV proxy.** Pixel entropy / edge density and audio loudness;
   ideal for post-hoc video analysis, unavailable to in-game pacing.
6. **Hybrid layered metric (likely recommendation).** Weighted object count
   (layer 1) + event window (layer 2) combined into a normalised,
   exponentially smoothed `actionIntensity` scalar plus a `burstiness`
   derivative — then persisted as a versioned time series feeding both
   pacing and video-editing consumers.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — **new**; the research + decision document
  this work item delivers.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — reference/cross-link for the scoring model
  and pacing rationale.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared entity
  registries (player bullets, enemy bullets, drops, enemies, explosions) that
  a future counter would read.
- `src/ai/` (world model / `BotSnapshot` builder) — predicted reuse point for
  the per-tick state vector.
- `src/core/runEndedSignal.ts`, `src/core/devScenario.ts` — precedents for a
  dev-gated game→tooling signal.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the video
  consumer that would join timestamps to captured WebM.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention
  any implementation must follow.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** — Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester
  telemetry (parent epic; telemetry infrastructure this builds on).
- **AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH** — Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state
  and events (child; `actionIntensity` field would live here).
- **AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO** — Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable
  sinks, consent flag (child; provides the sink/schema for the time series).
- **AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ** — Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling
  (consumer of the recorded action series).
- **AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4** — Same-seed evaluation harness (consumer for
  pacing/A-B metrics).
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Automated gameplay capture spike (video consumer;
  see `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`).
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** — Smart capture bot (emits the runs action
  intensity would be recorded against).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — duplicate instrumentation (scope creep).** Building a standalone
  counter would drift from the telemetry pipeline; mitigated by making
  telemetry integration AC4 and mandating reuse.
- **Risk — weights are subjective.** The seed weights may not reflect
  perceived excitement; mitigated by making the model **tunable/config-driven**
  and documenting the rationale per weight, with event-window and stress
  signals as cross-checks.
- **Risk — metric ≠ excitement.** Object count is at best a *proxy*; the
  document must state this explicitly and recommend calibration against
  human ratings or physiological data before it drives difficulty.
- **Risk — performance / bundle impact.** Mitigated by O(entities), sampling,
  and dev/opt-in gating.
- **Risk — capture de-sync.** Joining the JSONL series to captured WebM
  timestamps needs a shared clock anchor; record a run-start timestamp/seed.
- **Assumption —** the telemetry epic's per-tick state recording
  (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH) is the canonical integration point and remains
  `high` priority.
- **Assumption —** the metric is sampled, not stored per rendered frame, to
  bound file size (rate to be decided in the document, e.g. 10 Hz).
- **Scope-creep note:** pacing algorithms, ML excitement prediction and
  auto-editing are **consumers**, not deliverables of this item; captured as
  separate work items below if not already tracked.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Scope of this work item — research + decision only, or include a
  prototype implementation?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): *"just the research + decision + epic
  creation"*. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-08. → AC1, AC5, and the
  "no gameplay change" constraint.
- **Q2: Should action intensity be built on the telemetry pipeline
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) or standalone? Should the telemetry item's priority
  be raised?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): *"part of it, ensure the telemetry
  item is at least high priority"*. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-08.
  Verified: telemetry epic AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4, framework
  AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO and instrumentation AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH are already
  `high`. → AC4 and the reuse constraint.
- **Q3: Should the research refine the seed scoring weights, or treat them
  as definitive?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): *"refining included"*. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-10-08. → AC2.

## Problem

Running `npm run build` from a git worktree created by the implement skill fails at the `build-audio` step:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from /home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js
```

## Root cause

`scripts/build-audio.mjs` `resolveToneForge()` resolves the sibling checkout as `join(repoRoot, '..', 'ToneForge')`. Inside a worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) that path is `.worklog/worktrees/ToneForge`, which does not exist, so resolution falls through to `tf` on PATH (`node_modules/.bin/tf -> ../toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js`). That copy has no `tsx` dependency, so the CLI crashes.

When built from the main checkout the sibling path resolves correctly and the build succeeds.

## Workaround used

`TONEFORGE_CLI=/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js npm run build` (the sibling's `node_modules` has `tsx`).

## Expected behaviour

`npm run build` succeeds inside a worktree without requiring `TONEFORGE_CLI` to be set manually, since worktrees are the mandated implementation workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `npm run build` succeeds from a worktree with no `TONEFORGE_CLI` set.
- AC2: Sibling resolution is anchored to the main checkout (e.g. via the git common dir) rather than the worktree root.
- AC3: Existing `build-audio` tests still pass and the main-checkout build is unaffected.

## Summary

During a `dev`→`main` release (`/skill:ship release`), the audit-readiness gate's conservative in-gate remediation re-runs `audit_runner.py issue <id>` for a top-level `in_review` item whose stored audit is stale/missing/transient. For an item with a passing verdict the runner sets `needsProducerReview=yes` (by design, so the producer-review gate blocks until a human reviews).

The problem: if the item was **already producer-approved** (`needsProducerReview=false`) — the normal steady state after the producer has reviewed it — a content-unchanged re-audit nonetheless flips the flag back to `true` and immediately blocks the release at the producer-review gate (exit 9) and the final-validation sweep (exit 12).

## Example User Story

As a producer running a release, having already reviewed and approved every top-level work item, I want the release's automatic audit remediation not to re-open producer review for an item whose content I already approved, so that a stale audit does not silently re-block an otherwise shippable release.

## Observed

Release run on 2026-10-08 (AI_Hell, dev→main, v0.1.10 candidate):

- Item `AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1` (top-level `test-failure`, completed/in_review) had `needsProducerReview=false` for its **entire** recorded history (verified from the `refs/worklog/data` sync commits: false from creation 10:19 through the last pre-release sync at 11:16:27 UTC).
- The audit gate reported `auto-remediating AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1 (stale audit)` and `auto-remediated successfully` at 11:20:39 UTC.
- The producer-review gate then blocked with exit 9: `1 of 24 work item(s) need producer review`.
- `wl audit-show` confirms the fresh audit is green (`readyToClose: true`, content fingerprint unchanged).

## Expected Behaviour (candidate)

One or both of:

1. In-gate remediation should preserve an existing `needsProducerReview=false` approval when the item's content fingerprint is unchanged across the re-audit (only a genuine content change should re-open producer review); and/or
2. The producer-review gate should recognise a flag that was set by an in-gate remediation in the same run and not treat it as a fresh, un-reviewed requirement (e.g. compare against the pre-run approved state).

## Evidence / References

- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (in-gate remediation re-runs the audit; "the gate never calls wl update directly").
- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/audit-remediation.js` (bounded remediation; no flag preservation).
- `$(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~L11784: sets `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level passing audits).

## Acceptance Criteria

## Summary

During the v0.1.10 dev→main release, the ship skill's **non-blocking** post-release branch cleanup (run-release.js step 10, `runPostReleaseCleanup`) failed:

```
Post-release cleanup: enumerating branches...
  ⚠ Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.
Found 0 merged local branch(es) to clean up.
Post-release cleanup: pruning local branches...
  Pruned 0 local branch(es).
Post-release cleanup: pruning remote branches...
  ⚠ Remote branch pruning failed: delete_remote_branches.py failed
```

Re-running the same scripts manually immediately afterwards succeeded (`summarize_branches.py ~6s`, `delete_remote_branches.py ~6s`, both exit 0), so the failure is not a permanent environment problem.

## Likely Cause

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a **fixed** report path `${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json` (`run-release.js` ~L735). In a multi-agent environment (herdr) where more than one agent may run a release/cleanup concurrently, the fixed path races: one process can truncate/replace the file while another reads it, producing the "Failed to read summarize report" path, and the follow-on remote prune inherits the broken state.

## Expected Behaviour

- The post-release cleanup uses a unique temporary report path (e.g. `mkdtempSync`) so concurrent runs cannot clobber each other.
- A transient cleanup failure is retried once, and the warning names the deterministic remediation.

## Evidence / References

- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js` `runPostReleaseCleanup` (fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json`; `delete_remote_branches.py` invocation).
- `$(skill_path cleanup)/scripts/{summarize_branches,prune_local_branches,delete_remote_branches}.py` — all succeed standalone.
- Discovered during release v0.1.10 (`discovered-from:release-v0.1.10`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a unique temp path per run; a unit test with two concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py`/report read no longer silently reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct, actionable warning.
3. The cleanup remains non-blocking (never changes the release exit code).
data.title: Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

# Add a GitHub link to the main menu

## Problem statement

Players and contributors have no way to discover the project's source code from the game itself.

## Users

- **Player/Contributor:** Sees the game on-screen, wants to find the repo to report bugs, contribute, or learn more.
- **Reviewer/Tester:** Needs quick access to the source during code reviews or gameplay testing.

### User stories

- *As a player who enjoys the game, I can click/tap a visible link on the main menu to open the GitHub repository in a new browser tab, without losing my game session.*
- *As a keyboard user, I can Tab to the GitHub link on the main menu and press Enter to open it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Renders:** A GitHub link (`🐙  GitHub`) is rendered as text in the bottom-left corner of the main menu (`MenuScene`), below the subtitle and at the same Y position as the subtitle. It uses the existing `MENU_TEXT_COLOR` (#00ffff) with the same padding scheme as other buttons.
2. **AC2 — Click opens repo:** Pointer-down on the link opens `https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell` in a new browser tab (`_blank`) with `noopener,noreferrer` flags.
3. **AC3 — Keyboard-accessible:** The link is registered with `FocusManager` after the Leaderboard button (Tab order: Play Game → Watch Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → **GitHub** → Gym Scene Index). Enter/Space on the focused link triggers the same action as a pointer click. Hover highlights the text in `#88ffff` (matching the existing pointer-over pattern).
4. **AC4 — Constant:** The URL is a single exported `const GITHUB_REPO_URL = 'https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell'` in `src/core/constants.ts` (re-exported from `MenuScene` for testability), used as both the display label and the click target.
5. **AC5 — Tests:** Unit tests verify (a) the button renders with the correct label, (b) pointer activation calls `window.open` with the correct URL and target, and (c) keyboard activation via `FocusManager.handleKey` triggers the same `window.open` call.

## Constraints

- **Keyboard parity (GDD §2.1):** No mouse is ever required. The link must be in the Tab cycle.
- **No mouse required:** Use Phaser's existing pointer + keyboard interaction model; no DOM overlay.
- **New tab only:** Always use `_blank` to preserve the game session.
- **Existing pattern:** Must match the visual style of other menu buttons (neon-cyan text, dark background padding).
- **No `FocusManager` changes:** Reuse the existing manager; do not modify its public API.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` renders 5 controls: Play Game, Watch Demo, Settings, Leaderboard, Gym Scene Index (dev, bottom-right, fixed position).
- All 5 controls use `this.add.text()` with the same visual pattern (fontFamily: monospace, 20px, MENU_TEXT_COLOR, dark background padding).
- A shared `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) handles Tab/arrow cycling and Enter/Space activation.
- `window.open` has not been used in `src/` before; Phaser's canvas is the sole rendering surface.

## Desired change

Add a 6th control (`🐙  GitHub`) to the main menu:
- **Position:** Bottom-left, aligned near the bottom edge (X ≈ 16, Y ≈ GAME_HEIGHT − 12), matching the Gym Scene Index button's offset pattern.
- **Activation:** `window.open(GITHUB_REPO_URL, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` on both pointer and keyboard activation.
- **Tab order:** Between Leaderboard and Gym Scene Index.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Add the GitHub button (render, pointer handler, FocusManager registration).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Export `GITHUB_REPO_URL`.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — Add tests for the new button.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Popup blocker:** `window.open` must be called synchronously within the user-gesture event handler; otherwise the browser may block it. Mitigated by calling `window.open` directly in the pointer/keyboard handlers.
- **Tab order change:** Adds a 6th control to the existing 5. The order (Play → Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → GitHub → Gym Index) follows visual hierarchy (top→bottom, left→right).
- **Hardcoded URL:** The repo URL is a constant, not environment-configurable. Acceptable for a personal project; fork maintainers would edit the constant.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Where should the GitHub link live, and should it be keyboard-focusable? — Answer (operator): **A** — footer link, bottom-left, pointer-clickable and keyboard-focusable, appended to the Tab cycle. **Recommended** — keeps the GDD keyboard-parity contract intact.
- Q: How should activation behave? — Answer (operator): **A** — open in a new browser tab via `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`. **Recommended** — preserves the game session.
- Q: Where should the URL come from? — Answer (operator): **A** — single exported constant (`GITHUB_REPO_URL` in `src/core/constants.ts`), used for both label and click target. **Recommended** — testable, single source of truth.

## Related work

- **MenuScene Settings button** (AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N) — Similar pattern of adding a button to MenuScene.
- **In-game menu keyboard support (PauseScene)** (AH-0MUBZUQBL0080B88) — Keyboard navigation convention.
- **Add published game URL to top of README** (AH-0MUK3HYC3001YU05) — Same project URL, different location.
- **Create Main Menu scene** (AH-0MU72YVFR005VB2N) — Parent menu work.

# Batch scenario / multi-video capture tooling

## Problem statement

`npm run capture` produces exactly one video per invocation, and `--scenario`
accepts a single, unlisted value. There is no way to (a) discover which dev
scenarios exist, (b) run every scenario in one call, or (c) generate N videos
without a shell loop that pays the Vite + Chromium startup cost on every run.

**User stories:**

- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` to show every
  implemented dev scenario (name + one-line effect) so I do not have to read the
  source.
- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` to produce one
  video per scenario in a single command, reusing one Vite server and one
  browser session.
- As the maintainer, I want `npm run capture -- --count N` (optionally with
  `--scenario`) to produce N videos as review / regression evidence.
- As a producer/reviewer, I want a final batch summary and a non-zero exit when
  any item fails, so a batch can gate CI.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `parseCaptureArgs`: a single `scenario`
  string; flags are `--duration`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup`,
  `--output`, `--port`, `--headed`, `--json`, `--keep-server`, `--scripted`,
  `--scenario`.
- `runCapture` boots one Vite dev server + one Chromium browser per invocation
  and writes one output WebM.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` is the game-side resolver: `boss`, `boss-four-hits`,
  `defeat` (plus the default no-scenario demo run). The Node capture tool does
  not import it; `--scenario` is passed through the URL unvalidated (an unknown
  value silently runs the normal demo).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the three scenario values in a table.
- There is no `--list-scenarios`, `--all-scenarios` or `--count`, and no shared
  scenario registry between the game and the Node tool.

## Desired change

1. **Scenario registry (single source).** Add a shared, pure scenario registry
   (name + short description) usable by both the game resolver and the Node
   capture tool, so the list cannot drift. Likely a browser-free `.mjs` module
   (mirroring `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`) that `src/core/devScenario.ts`
   consumes.
2. **`--list-scenarios`.** Print the implemented scenarios in human-readable
   form, or machine-readable JSON with `--json`; exit 0 without booting
   Vite/Chromium.
3. **`--all-scenarios`.** Run every registered scenario in one invocation, one
   video each, continuing past a per-item failure and reporting a per-item plus
   aggregate result.
4. **`--count N`.** Produce N videos (the default demo run, or N of a given
   `--scenario`).
5. **Single-session batch.** Reuse one Vite server and one Chromium browser
   across the batch, with a fresh page/context per item so a failed clip cannot
   poison the next.
6. **Output naming.** Deterministic, collision-free default names per item;
   document how `--output` behaves for batches (directory or prefix).
7. **Summary + exit code.** Final summary (path, outcome, complete/capHit,
   bytes per item); exit non-zero if any item failed or hit the cap.
8. **Backwards compatibility.** A single `--scenario` invocation behaves exactly
   as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (list):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists every implemented
  scenario (value + one-line effect) from the shared registry, exits 0, and
  boots no browser or server; `--json` emits a machine-readable array.
- **AC2 (all):** `npm run capture -- --all-scenarios` produces one video per
  registered scenario in a single invocation and reports success/failure per
  item.
- **AC3 (count):** `npm run capture -- --count N` produces exactly N videos
  (N >= 1); with `--scenario S` all N use S, otherwise the default demo run;
  `--count 0`, missing or non-numeric values error clearly.
- **AC4 (single session):** across a batch the Vite server and Chromium browser
  start exactly once (asserted via instrumentation/count), with a fresh
  page/context per item.
- **AC5 (naming):** items get deterministic, collision-free default output
  paths; an existing file is never silently overwritten by a different item.
- **AC6 (summary/exit):** a batch prints a final aggregate summary and exits
  non-zero if any item failed or hit the cap; a single-item failure does not
  abort the remaining items.
- **AC7 (tests):** hermetic unit tests cover arg parsing (`--list-scenarios`,
  `--all-scenarios`, `--count`, combinations and invalid input), the registry
  contents, output-name generation, and batch result/exit-code aggregation
  (no browser); existing capture tests continue to pass.
- **AC8 (docs):** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the `README.md` capture
  section document the list/all/count flags with examples; `--help` updated.
- **AC9 (suite):** `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Constraints

- Capture stays outside the shipped bundle; the shared registry must be
  browser-free and consumed by dev-gated code only.
- The browser/encode path cannot run under vitest (the canvas is stubbed), so
  all new decision logic (registry, naming, aggregation) must be pure and
  unit-tested; the browser path is exercised by `npm run capture`.
- Serial-by-default batched execution (one browser) to avoid host resource
  contention.
- Existing single-scenario, `--duration` and `--scripted` behaviour unchanged.

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** the three registered scenarios (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`,
  `defeat`) stay the complete set. Because the registry becomes the single
  source, a future scenario added in `src/core/devScenario.ts` without
  registering it would drift from the CLI. Mitigation: make the game resolver
  consume the registry and add a registry <-> resolver test.
- **Failure mode:** a per-item browser/encode failure must not poison the
  shared session (one Vite server + one Chromium browser). Mitigation: a fresh
  page/context per item, per-item error capture, and continue to the next item
  (AC6).
- **Failure mode:** deterministic default batch names could collide on a
  re-run, or an existing file could be silently overwritten by a different
  item. Mitigation: item-scoped, collision-free names plus a never-silently-
  overwrite check (AC5).
- **Failure mode:** a batch item that never signals a run-end could hang.
  Mitigation: the existing per-item `--max-duration` cap bounds each item and
  the summary reports `capHit` per item (AC6).
- **Risk (host resources):** parallel capture would exhaust CPU/GPU on the dev
  host, so execution stays serial by default (one browser; see Constraints).
- **Assumption:** `--list-scenarios` must not boot Vite/Chromium, so the
  registry has to be importable by bare Node — a browser-free `.mjs` module
  following the `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs` precedent.
- **Scope-creep risk:** ad-hoc extras (a `--filter` flag, per-scenario duration
  overrides, an HTML index page) are out of scope; record each as a
  `discovered-from` work item rather than widening this change.

## OPEN QUESTIONs (non-blocking, recommended defaults)

- Should `--all-scenarios` include the default no-scenario demo run?
  *Recommended:* NO (an explicit `--include-demo` opt-in), because the demo is
  non-deterministic and multi-minute.
- `--output` in a batch: treat it as a directory (*recommended*) or a filename
  prefix?
- Should `--count` combine with `--all-scenarios` (N repeats of every scenario)?
  *Recommended:* reject the combination, or define it explicitly as N x all.
  Directed to the producer at plan/implement time.

## Key files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — flags, batch orchestration, summary/exit
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.d.mts` — types for new exports
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`) — shared browser-free scenario
  registry (or extend `capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — consume the shared registry
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — hermetic tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md` — documentation

## Related work

- **Create full video playthroughs** (AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU) — `discovered-from`;
  added the full-run capture and the `defeat` scenario this builds on.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic ...** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  `related-to`; the capture epic.
- **Spike: automated gameplay video capture** (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — the
  pipeline this extends.

## Appendix: clarification

- The operator asked (this session) whether scenarios can be listed, all
  generated in one call, and N videos generated; none of the three exists today.
  This work item adds them. Approval to write code has NOT been given
  (create-only).
- Q (intake evaluation, this session, Map): "Is the work item defined well
  enough to skip the interactive interview?" — Answer (agent, Map): "Yes. The
  brief already carries a problem statement, user stories, 9 measurable ACs,
  constraints, key files and related work; an interactive interview would only
  repeat information already recorded in the work item." Source: `wl show
  AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP --json`; repo inspection of
  `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/capture-run-lifecycle.mjs`,
  `src/core/devScenario.ts`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md`.
- OPEN QUESTION (retained for plan/implement; non-blocking, no answer supplied
  this session): demo inclusion in `--all-scenarios` (preferred **NO**;
  `--include-demo` opt-in), `--output` batch semantics (preferred a
  **directory**), and `--count` combined with `--all-scenarios` (preferred
  **reject**, or define as N x all). The recommended defaults are advisory; the
  producer's choice at plan time wins.
- Related-work research (find-related, this session): appended the automated
  report below (`AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`, `AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123`,
  `AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C` plus three repo file matches); the manual **Related
  work** section above remains authoritative.

- **AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN** – Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (open)
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123** – Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen (completed)
